title: arXiv Physics — Daily notable papers, Friday 20 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This is an inferred ordering of notable recent papers, not a measured popularity or readership ranking. At the snapshot, Semantic Scholar recorded zero citation and influential-citation totals for every selected paper; popularity evidence is therefore limited, and selection relies on concrete results, publication/collaboration status, cross-listing, and data or methods.

sections.title: Gamma-Ray Pulsar Discovery Using a Lattice-Based Method
sections.abstract: Using a high-dimensional lattice search on 15 years of Fermi-LAT data, the authors report the first gamma-ray pulsar found with this method, PSR J1622−7204, at 261 Hz, with about ten CPU hours of search time.
sections.claimed_result: The authors identify an isolated 261-Hz gamma-ray pulsar in Fermi-LAT photon data and argue that the search method could make blind searches, including some binary searches, more practical.
sections.evidence_type: observational; computational lattice search of Fermi-LAT Pass 8 photon arrival times and weights
sections.unique_caveat: The authors estimate success in only about 1% of randomly selected 80-photon subsets; the demonstrated search assumes an isolated pulsar and a simplified pulse profile, and binary-pulsar discovery remains a prospect rather than a demonstrated result.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: First successful Fermi-LAT demonstration of the method, large reported compute reduction relative to prior search, and publication in Physical Review Letters (DOI 10.1103/vlt2-xzgk).

sections.title: Progress in measurements of the CKM angle γ and charm mixing at LHCb
sections.abstract: The LHCb collaboration combines measurements from 2011–2018 with its first γ measurement using 2024 data, reporting updated precision values for the CKM angle, charm mixing, and CP-violation parameters.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report γ = (63.2 +2.3/−2.2)° modulo 180°, with charm-mixing and CP-violation parameters described as the most precise to date.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; combined LHCb measurements using 2011–2018 data and the first γ measurement from 2024 data
sections.unique_caveat: The results are a combination rather than a new-physics discovery; the interpretation of CP asymmetries depends on assumptions about charm-decay contributions, and γ is determined modulo 180°.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Large experimental collaboration combines its first γ result from 2024 data with prior measurements; complete figures and supporting material are linked through CERN's public LHCb analysis page.

sections.title: The gravitational wave candidate S251112cm: near-complete optical coverage with ATLAS, Pan-STARRS and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory
sections.abstract: The authors combine ATLAS, Pan-STARRS, Rubin, and follow-up observations of the subsolar-mass merger candidate S251112cm, finding no convincing optical counterpart and excluding specified kilonova and supernova models over about 80% of the localization volume.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find no convincing counterpart and report that the combined Pan-STARRS and Rubin observations exclude AT 2017gfo-like kilonova and SN 1998bw-like Type Ic-BL models in roughly 80% of the 90% localization region.
sections.evidence_type: observational; optical transient searches, survey coverage and limits, host-galaxy distance information, and VLT spectroscopy
sections.unique_caveat: S251112cm is itself a gravitational-wave candidate, not a confirmed merger; the exclusion depends on assumed counterpart light curves and brightness ranges, and some residual candidates lack distances. The result is not evidence that no fainter or different counterpart existed.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Multi-survey campaign combines ATLAS, Pan-STARRS, Rubin, and VLT follow-up, quantifies broad limits, is submitted to MNRAS, and has public Rubin observing documentation in a GCN circular.

sections.title: False Periodicities in Repeating Fast Radio Bursts Caused by Burst Clustering
sections.abstract: A sliding-window search and waiting-time-preserving randomizations of four active repeaters show that burst clustering can reproduce apparent short-period candidates, leaving no robust evidence for an intrinsic short period in these data.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find that candidate periods in four highly active repeating FRBs can arise from non-Poissonian burst clustering and do not establish a coherent rotation period.
sections.evidence_type: computational; sliding-window and randomized-null analyses of burst times from four repeating FRB sources, plus rotation-modulated aftershock-sequence simulations
sections.unique_caveat: The analysis concerns four highly active repeaters and the tested time ranges; it does not rule out rotation-related periodicity in every FRB source or at all timescales.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Accepted for publication in ApJ and directly tests a reported 1.7-second periodicity using a waiting-time-preserving randomization and a complementary simulated null model.

sections.title: Every galaxy is a radio source: a stellar-mass dependent minimum 150 MHz luminosity identified in the LoTSS Deep Fields
sections.abstract: Using LoTSS Deep Fields radio data and SED-based properties for 113,228 galaxies, the authors find a stellar-mass-dependent floor in faint 150-MHz emission and interpret it as evidence that weak accretion can contribute to radio luminosity usually associated with star formation.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a mass-dependent minimum luminosity around 10²⁰–10²² W Hz⁻¹, independent of SFR in the relevant regime, and find that a two-component star-formation plus weak-AGN model fits the observed trends.
sections.evidence_type: observational; LoTSS Deep Fields DR2 ELAIS-N1 radio imaging plus Prospector-derived stellar masses and star-formation rates
sections.unique_caveat: Weak accretion is an interpretation of population trends rather than a direct AGN identification for each galaxy; inferred accretion rates depend on scaling relations, and faint residual AGN contamination may remain.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Accepted for publication in MNRAS and analyzes 113,228 galaxies using LoTSS Deep Fields DR2 150-MHz data, with implications for low-frequency SFR estimates and future LOFAR/SKA surveys.

sections.title: A Surrogate Detector Model for the MINERvA Open Dataset
sections.abstract: The authors train a probabilistic surrogate on MINERvA open simulation data to map neutrino interaction final states into reconstructed observables, including a holdout test and forward-folding of three event generators.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report that the surrogate reproduces the withheld interaction’s reconstructed response within estimated uncertainties and reproduces MINERvA selection efficiencies and purities in an end-to-end analysis.
sections.evidence_type: computational; probabilistic detector-response model trained on the MINERvA open simulation dataset and applied to inclusive charged-current muon-neutrino data
sections.unique_caveat: Validation is against the available MINERvA simulation and detector-response conditions; the holdout test is not an independent measurement of a new interaction channel or proof of transfer to other detectors.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Addresses the open-data detector-response bottleneck; tests withheld two-particle–two-hole interactions and compares GENIE, NuWro, and GiBUU predictions in reconstructed space.

sections.title: Square Kilometre Array Science Data Challenge 3b: EoR inference
sections.abstract: The authors compare 16 teams’ estimates of the neutral hydrogen fraction using shared simulated SKA Epoch-of-Reionization data and find substantial pipeline-to-pipeline variation, even in a relatively simple noise-only case.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find significant inter-team variation in inferred neutral fractions across redshift bins, while the combined mean estimates remain close to the simulation inputs.
sections.evidence_type: computational; 16 teams’ inference pipelines applied to simulated SKA data across multiple foreground, power-spectrum, imaging, and reionization scenarios
sections.unique_caveat: The comparison is based on simulations, not observed EoR detections; a close ensemble average can coexist with biased individual methods and does not by itself identify which pipeline is reliable.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: SKAO-organized nine-month community challenge with common simulated datasets and 16 teams; the manuscript is submitted to MNRAS and makes inter-method variability explicit.

sections.title: First Ωm–w Measurement Using Only Fast Radio Burst Observations
sections.abstract: The authors use a cosmology-dependent matter-spectrum emulator and electron model to infer Ωm and the dark-energy equation-of-state parameter w from 125 localized FRBs without external observational priors on those parameters.
sections.claimed_result: Under flat wCDM, the authors infer Ωm = 0.33 +0.10/−0.11 and w = −0.80 +0.28/−0.38, with a positive Ωm–w degeneracy that differs from the Type Ia supernova constraint direction.
sections.evidence_type: observational; statistical inference from localized-FRB dispersion measures, using a nonlinear matter-power-spectrum emulator and an electron-distribution prescription
sections.unique_caveat: The parameter constraints are broad and depend on modeling the cosmic, host, and intervening-electron contributions to dispersion measure; the abstract presents a preprint result, not an independent cosmological consensus.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-lists cosmology and high-energy astrophysics and reports a first FRB-only simultaneous two-parameter inference from 125 localized sources, with explicit uncertainties.

sections.title: Equation of state of hot and dense QCD at the physical point via the complex Langevin equation
sections.abstract: Using complex-Langevin lattice simulations, the authors calculate continuum-extrapolated thermodynamic quantities for physical-point 2+1+1-flavor QCD at high temperature and baryon chemical potential.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report baryon density, pressure, sound speed, and adiabatic compressibility for temperatures of 260–600 MeV and baryon chemical potentials up to μB/T ≲ 10.
sections.evidence_type: computational; 2+1+1-flavor lattice-QCD simulations using the complex Langevin equation, with continuum extrapolation
sections.unique_caveat: The paper marks the largest-chemical-potential region as increasingly unreliable because lattice saturation spoils the continuum fit; the results are also a conference-proceedings contribution rather than an independent method comparison.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across lattice, phenomenological, and theoretical high-energy physics; finite-density method extends toward μB/T ≲ 10 and is a Lattice 2026 proceedings contribution.

sections.title: The Galaxy Activity, Torus, and Outflow Survey: N. Little Red Dots are not dust deficient: constraints from Seyfert 1 JWST spectra
sections.abstract: The authors scale nearby Seyfert 1 JWST spectra against a stack of 249 high-redshift Little Red Dots and find that a reddened accretion disc plus a low-reprocessing-efficiency torus can reproduce their optical-to-infrared energy balance.
sections.claimed_result: The authors argue that the LRDs need not be dust-deficient if their accretion discs are more reddened and their tori reprocess less radiation than local Seyfert 1 tori.
sections.evidence_type: observational; JWST spectra of nearby Seyfert 1 nuclei compared with stacked NIRSpec/MIRI spectra of high-redshift LRDs and SED modeling
sections.unique_caveat: The inference transfers a local Seyfert template to a heterogeneous high-redshift population; the authors report agreement within a factor of three in near-infrared emission and require different reddening and torus efficiency from local Seyferts.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Uses rest-frame JWST 3–27 μm spectra and a 249-object stack; submitted to A&A, with the stacks and models deposited in Zenodo.

sections.title: Little Red Dots from Primordial Vacuum Bubbles
sections.abstract: The authors propose that rare vacuum bubbles nucleated during inflation could form 10⁶–10⁸-solar-mass primordial black holes at an abundance compatible with JWST’s Little Red Dots, without invoking the enhanced curvature perturbations excluded by CMB spectral-distortion limits.
sections.claimed_result: The authors show that a narrow, adjustable primordial-black-hole mass spectrum can match the bright-LRD abundance while satisfying the leading accretion constraint in their model.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; inflationary vacuum-bubble nucleation and primordial-black-hole abundance/constraint modeling
sections.unique_caveat: The result depends on the assumed inflationary tunneling history, bubble abundance, and black-hole formation model; it does not establish that LRDs are primordial black holes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-lists cosmology, gravitation, and particle phenomenology and offers a quantitatively constrained early-Universe mechanism for LRD abundance; it is a theoretical proposal, not observational evidence.
